task:
Optimize the supplied standalone LIBXSMM SME CPU kernel for row-major FP32 C=A@B.
Target strictly >1800 GFLOP/s under the unchanged kernel-opt hill. ABI:
void gemm(int n,const float*A,const float*B,float*C). Main timing n512; preserve
correct general sizes/tails and n<=0. Fixed Apple clang21 flags:
-O3 -march=native -ffast-math -shared -fPIC -lm. Tolerance .002. Single thread,
no external runtime libraries, mixed precision, result/input caching, or scorer edits.
All calls, packing, allocations, SME state transitions, and stores remain timed.
Preserve the complete LIBXSMM BSD license notice. Inputs are fresh on every call.

Current baseline still invokes the original full512 LIBXSMM kernel once. Its source
now includes an OPTIONAL UNUSED offline-generated helper, sera_libxsmm_panel32,
whose exported shape is colmajor M512,N32,K512,lda/ldb/ldc512,beta0,no transpose.
The helper's body is1536 exact generated bytes; it has passed12 deterministic public
panel ABI correctness tests and an internal-branch/no-relocation/no-external-call audit.
The whole augmented baseline passed48 correctness cases. It is a new build identity,
so Sera measures a fresh baseline. No helper performance is yet known.

The helper is declared before gemm and defined as embedded assembly afterward.
It takes const void* parameters[22], with [4]=column-major A pointer,[10]=B,[16]=C;
all remaining fields zero. For row-major 32-row output band starting at r:
parameters[4]=B; parameters[10]=A+r*512; parameters[16]=C+r*512.
Sixteen disjoint bands r=0,32,...,480 cover the full product. This is a legal optional
layout experiment, not a mandatory choice or a measured win. Each call internally
packs the corresponding A row panel into64KiB and enters/exits SME. The original
full512 path packs64 rows into128KiB and does one overall SME entry. Compare the
cache/packing tradeoff against the extra call/state-transition overhead; do not infer
speedup from buffer size alone. Using the helper can be expressed as a small guarded
wrapper edit, without rewriting the long generated assembly. Astra must implement
any selected wrapper and the evaluator will test the full GEMM, not merely a panel.

The 15 Luna specialists jointly propose and rank the next experiments. Astra selects
roles, implements the selected queue, and reviews the measured results. Concrete
layout/packing hypotheses are welcome; do not repeat previously measured instruction
scheduling sources. Roles can propose different legal ways to use the source and
helper, but duplicate descriptions are not distinct experiments. Name exact source
blocks and coordinate all pointer, stride, layout, and traversal changes needed.
Do not constrain a larger layout change to preserve incompatible old strides.
The helper and baseline are imported reference code, not a Sera-discovered improvement.
Only a changed source that passes fresh paired gates can demonstrate an improvement.

Prior phases below are historical context only; never use them as fresh controls.
Retain all AC/battery data separately. This block requires its initial power mode and
settings throughout. The per-agent timeout remains180 seconds, with108 calls,
six total implementation attempts, and1800 seconds overall for this new block.

{"generator-review-luna.md": "# Pinned LIBXSMM SME generator: legal layout and blocking controls\n\n**Source facts.** This review uses LIBXSMM commit [`10490f10e79d4511f252c33279ef970a188cfab6`](https://github.com/libxsmm/libxsmm/tree/10490f10e79d4511f252c33279ef970a188cfab6). The offline exporter in [`export_kernel.c`](../cpu-libxsmm-reference-2026-09-24/export_kernel.c) dispatches an FP32 `(M,N,K)=(512,512,512)` kernel with `BETA_0` and no prefetch, then exports the generated code bytes. Runtime LIBXSMM is not needed for a generated kernel.\n\nAt M4, `generator_gemm.c` selects the SME GEMM path only for FP32 and a restricted flag set: XGEMM ABI, optional `TRANS_A`, `TRANS_B`, and batch-reduce-stride; it strips `BETA_0` before checking that set ([source](https://github.com/libxsmm/libxsmm/blob/10490f10e79d4511f252c33279ef970a188cfab6/src/generator_gemm.c#L1284-L1299)). `generator_gemm_common_aarch64.c` hard-codes macro blocking at N=64 and M=32 ([source](https://github.com/libxsmm/libxsmm/blob/10490f10e79d4511f252c33279ef970a188cfab6/src/generator_gemm_common_aarch64.c#L2306-L2321)). There is no public descriptor field or SME-specific environment variable for choosing those block sizes. `LIBXSMM_TARGET` and `libxsmm_set_target_arch` select the code-generation architecture, not blocking.\n\n`TRANS_A` and `TRANS_B` are legal descriptor choices, and `generator_gemm_sme.c` contains A/B transpose-to-stack paths. For example, no `TRANS_B` invokes `transpose_b_to_stack` in the 17\u201332 N remainder path; setting `TRANS_B` skips that step there ([source](https://github.com/libxsmm/libxsmm/blob/10490f10e79d4511f252c33279ef970a188cfab6/src/generator_gemm_sme.c#L1308-L1334)). A flag flip alone changes the mathematical operation. It is legal for this fixed workload only if the supplied operand storage and leading dimensions are changed to match the flag while preserving beta=0 output.\n\n## Concrete generator-supported decomposition\n\nThe SME generator has a direct N=32 path: with N=32, its `n_rest` falls in `17..32`, then it uses M blocks of 32, calls the same SME outer-product kernel, and handles beta-zero C initialization/store ([source](https://github.com/libxsmm/libxsmm/blob/10490f10e79d4511f252c33279ef970a188cfab6/src/generator_gemm_sme.c#L1308-L1428)). This enables an offline-generated `(512,32,512)` primitive without editing LIBXSMM or introducing a runtime library. A wrapper can cover the original row-major output in 16 disjoint row bands, with call index `r=0,32,...,480`:\n\n- `A_arg = B`, interpreted column-major as `B\u1d40` (`m=512,k=512`);\n- `B_arg = A + r*512`, interpreted column-major as the 512x32 panel from 32 row-major rows of A;\n- `C_arg = C + r*512`, the matching 32 output rows; keep `lda=ldb=ldc=512`.\n\nThis is the identity `C\u1d40=B\u1d40A\u1d40` with the same FP32 values and beta=0 semantics. The generator will still pack its non-transposed B operand to stack once per primitive call. Compared with one 512x512 call, this trades sixteen function/SME entries for a narrower generated kernel and per-call panel packing. Whether that helps is an untested hypothesis; include every pack and call in timing and verify panel boundaries/correctness.\n\n## What can change, and what cannot\n\n1. **Descriptor/layout choices:** export `TRANS_A` or `TRANS_B` variants only with matching packed input and leading dimensions. The M4 generator accepts these variants, but direct use of the current row-major pointers with toggled flags is incorrect. A prepacked operand plus `TRANS_B` may bypass the generator's internal B transpose in relevant paths; this is a data-layout experiment, not a free flag optimization.\n2. **Public blocking route:** export smaller N shapes such as N=32 and loop over disjoint output panels in the wrapper. The source has a dedicated 17\u201332 branch, but the wrapper adds calls and cannot claim a gain in advance.\n3. **Internal blocking:** to change the fixed 32/64 macro-block constants while keeping a single full-shape dispatch requires an offline LIBXSMM source modification and regeneration. It must update the paired M/N remainder logic and pack/store traversal, not only `setup_blocking_sme`. Do not expect `LIBXSMM_TARGET` or a leading-dimension choice to select new block sizes.\n\nThe adapter remains specialized to the fixed n=512 call and must preserve the existing general-size fallback. This note reports generator capabilities and algebraic legality only; it contains no benchmark result or performance promise.\n", "layout-review-luna.md": "# Layout option for the next specialist board\n\nThe latest completed continuation did not measure an A/B data-layout change. It measured three K-loop schedule variants; none met the promotion gate. The `a_transpose` implementation timed out, and the selected `scratch_lifetime` attempt abstained because \u201cshrink scratch to 64 KiB\u201d conflicted with keeping the current 128 KiB consumer strides and 64-row traversal. That is a useful constraint: a smaller buffer only works if packing, consumer stride, tile coverage, and traversal change together. See the [continuation summary](../cpu-libxsmm-next-continue-2026-09-25/README.md), [saved swarm state](../cpu-libxsmm-next-continue-2026-09-25/agent/state.json), and [measured trials](../cpu-libxsmm-next-continue-2026-09-25/search/result.json).\n\nOne bounded layout experiment for specialists to assess is a **32-row A panel path for n=512**, implemented in C/SME and selected only by the existing `n==512` dispatch. It avoids rewriting the long embedded LIBXSMM loop body. The current fast path allocates 128 KiB of stack scratch per 64-row band (`kernel.c`, `Llibxsmm_64`, lines 69\u201375) and consumes its packed A data with a 256-byte per-K pointer step (`Llibxsmm_478`/`Llibxsmm_70c`, lines 318\u2013345 and 482\u2013509). The general fallback already has a ZA transpose helper and four-tile SME GEMM structure (`sme_transpose` and `sme_gemm`, lines 681\u2013751), but it materializes a full 512-by-512 transpose.\n\nThe proposed experiment would replace the 512-only dispatch with a row-panel loop that packs one 32-row A block into a reusable 64 KiB scratch panel, then computes all 16 output-column tiles before reusing that panel:\n\n```text\nfor r0 in 0, 32, ..., 480:\n    pack[k, r] = A[r0 + r, k]        # k=0..511, r=0..31; 16,384 FP32 values\n    for j0 in 0, 32, ..., 480:\n        zero one 32x32 ZA output tile\n        for k in 0..511, increasing:\n            load A panel values pack[k, 0..31]\n            load contiguous B row values B[k, j0..j0+31]\n            apply the same four FP32 FMOPA updates\n        store C[r0..r0+31, j0..j0+31]\n```\n\nThis defines the data layout and loop order together. The packed address is `pack[k*32 + r]`; the input is `A[(r0+r)*512 + k]`; B remains in its current row-major form, so each 32-value B slice is contiguous; and C is written at `C[(r0+r)*512 + (j0+c)]`. A K iteration must load the 32 A values and 32 B values for the same `k`, update all four ZA tiles in the existing accumulation order, and advance K exactly once. Every output tile has one writer, starts from zero, and stores 32 rows by 32 columns. The row panels cover `[0,512)` without overlap or gaps. Keep the current ABI and `n!=512` fallback unchanged.\n\nThe scratch buffer is allocated once inside `gemm`, reused for all sixteen row panels, and freed before return. If allocation fails, dispatch to the unchanged LIBXSMM 512 kernel. Packing, compute, fallback handling, and cleanup all remain in the timed call. Do not keep the old 256-byte consumer stride or two-half traversal while shrinking the panel: this panel is dense K-major with a 128-byte K step, and the new 32-row loop owns one row half at a time.\n\nThe hypothesis is narrower scratch and explicit reuse of each packed A panel across every output-column tile. The main risk is that 32-row panels may reload B more often than the current 64-row blocking; the full packing and allocation cost also counts. Current evidence gives no speedup or cache-causality claim. Specialists should decide whether this trade-off merits a candidate, and whether the existing transpose helper can be adapted safely to produce the 32-row panel or whether a simpler pack is safer. Preserve the fixed FP32 arithmetic, full-call timing, tail/general fallback behavior, tolerance, and existing repeated paired-control gates.\n", "measurement-review-luna.md": "# LIBXSMM timing evidence review\n\nThis review uses public signed `kernel-opt` reports, their saved before/after host observations, and the phase verification records. It does not use private evaluator inputs or rerun measurements.\n\n## Finding\n\nThe evidence does not identify a compute bottleneck. It shows substantial timing variation for the same source under unchanged benchmark settings, while recording no per-kernel counters or stage timings. This is consistent with run-to-run noise or changing runtime state, but the records do not establish which one caused it. They cannot distinguish a compute limit from a memory, packing, scheduling, or thermal limit.\n\nEach official report contains three raw durations and scores the fastest (`seconds_best_of_3`). Those timings are only about 0.16\u20130.50 ms. The report prints decimal values to nanosecond places, but gives no calibrated timer resolution or accuracy. The observed spread among the three measurements is often tens to hundreds of microseconds, far larger than the last printed decimal places. The fastest-of-three score therefore hides much of the short-run spread and is not a stable estimate of typical call time.\n\n## Same-source evidence\n\nAll three phases used the frozen `kernel-opt` tree `76db49356748c18dccac376bed489268b047b60a`, n=512, tolerance 0.002, Apple clang 21 with `-O3 -march=native -ffast-math -shared -fPIC -lm`, and an arm64 Darwin report environment. The reference source SHA-256 is `7e9ab1076777a40cb0ad30527e381b221d4024cd99f370708971fb652b31810e`. The two AC baseline blocks and the battery baseline map to the same Hill submission hash, so their baseline results are for the same source.\n\n| Phase | Power captured before and after | Same-source baseline GFLOP/s, in report order | Fastest-of-three durations |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| AC reference | AC Power | 1541.3, 1333.3, 1328.1 | 174.2\u2013202.1 \u00b5s |\n| Separate AC swarm baseline | AC Power | 1643.5, 1276.7, 1176.1 | 163.3\u2013228.3 \u00b5s |\n| Battery swarm baseline | Battery Power | 1020.5, 1077.3, 1056.0 | 249.2\u2013263.0 \u00b5s |\n\nThese phase vectors are kept separate. In particular, the AC blocks are separate runs, and the battery phase occurred later. Their absolute differences do not isolate a causal power-source effect. The power metadata does show normal OS mode differences: `powermode 0` on AC and `powermode 1` on battery. Each host capture reports no recorded thermal or performance warning. No capture reports clock frequency, core affinity, P/E core identity, active processes, or CPU utilization.\n\nThe within-report raw timing arrays also vary. Across the AC baselines, individual timings range from 163.3 to 335.0 \u00b5s. Across the battery baseline and its paired unchanged controls, individual timings range from 249.2 to 414.8 \u00b5s. In the battery block, the unchanged source's initial validation scores were 1020.5\u20131077.3 GFLOP/s, while its nine paired-control scores ranged from 795.1 to 1040.1 GFLOP/s. The candidate score changes must be judged against those contemporaneous controls, not against AC scores or an earlier battery baseline.\n\n## Candidate evidence limits\n\nBattery candidate sources were measured only in the battery block; none has an AC candidate measurement. The selected experiment conflicts with its preservation requirements. Both existing K loops advance scratch by 256 bytes per K step and rewind 131072 bytes. The first 32-row tile alone accesses through scratch byte 130943, so reducing allocation to 65536 bytes without changing consumption would exceed bounds. The current traversal computes both 32-row halves for each B panel before advancing that panel. Computing all B panels for the first half before repacking the second half changes that traversal. A working 64 KiB design therefore requires changes to scratch stride, rewinds, second-half addressing, and compute traversal outside the permitted allocation/packing block. I cannot implement all stated requirements together or substitute a different experiment. No source changes or tests were performed.
